The gap

The material
nobody quotes.

Waste contractors are set up for predictable streams. Clean cardboard. Sorted plastics. General waste. The moment a material is bonded, oversized, contaminated or carrying your brand, it falls outside the service. It gets quoted as landfill, or it doesn't get quoted at all.

Meanwhile it sits in your racking, and the cost of it never appears on a waste invoice.

RISK 01

Brand exposure

Product that reaches a landfill floor intact can be pulled off it, resold, or photographed with your logo still on it.

RISK 02

Warehouse drag

Rejected stock ties up racking, floor space and forklift hours for months while someone works out what to do with it. That someone has a day job.

RISK 03

Reporting gaps

Landfill disposal produces no recovery data. If you report on diversion, packaging obligations or Scope 3, unprocessed material is a hole in the numbers.

RISK 04

Escalating cost

Landfill levies go up every year, and mixed waste pays the highest gate rate in the schedule.

Who we work with

Who calls us.

Manufacturing & Operations

Recurring production waste

Offcuts, rejected components and by-products generated on the same line every week. You need a repeatable, costed program — not a skip and a phone call.

Supply Chain & Quality

Defective & recalled product

Stock that cannot be sold, returned or reworked. You need it destroyed properly, evidenced, and off your balance sheet without becoming a brand incident.

Retail & Distribution

Obsolete and damaged stock

Discontinued lines, damaged returns and end-of-range inventory that must be permanently removed from circulation rather than quietly leaking into secondary markets.

Sustainability & ESG

Diversion you can evidence

You need recovery outcomes you can put in a report and defend — tonnages, destinations and processing method, not a generic "recycled responsibly" claim.

Waste & Recycling Operators

Streams you can't process

Material that arrives at your facility outside your equipment's capability. SHRED works as processing capacity behind you rather than in competition with you.

Facilities & Site Management

Accumulated legacy material

Years of stored material across a yard, warehouse or decommissioned site that has to be cleared, sorted and processed as a defined project.

Chain of custody

Gone, and provable.

With recalled, branded or defective product, the real risk is the product turning up again. The disposal cost is a footnote. SHRED runs these projects as a controlled chain, and what you get back is a documented outcome, not a weighbridge docket.

The controlled chain

  • Sealed collectionMaterial is loaded, secured and manifested at your site with item counts recorded against the agreed scope.
  • Direct to processingConsignments are directed to the nominated processing site without intermediate handling or resale exposure.
  • Irreversible size reductionProduct is shredded or granulated to a state where the item cannot be reconstituted, identified or resold.
  • Documented outcomeYou receive processing records covering quantity, method and destination for each consignment.

What you receive

Reporting is agreed at scoping stage and issued on completion. Available outputs include:

Consignment manifest Weighbridge records Processing method statement Certificate of destruction [confirm] Diversion & recovery summary Downstream destination record Witnessed destruction [confirm]

Why it matters

Your quality, legal and sustainability people all want the same thing: proof of what happened to it. A weighbridge docket doesn't give them that. Processing records do.

Applications

The calls we get.

Bedding manufacturer

"We generate rejected pocket springs and foam offcuts every week and it's all going to landfill."

SHRED assesses whether the stream can be separated at volume and converted into a recurring, costed processing program with monthly recovery reporting — rather than a weekly waste charge that grows with the levy.

Manufacturer — defective product

"We have multiple pallets of product that failed QA and cannot be sold or reworked."

SHRED assesses the product's construction and develops a destruction and separation plan that renders the item unusable, recovers what can be recovered, and documents the outcome for your quality and legal teams.

Retailer / distributor

"This range is discontinued. It cannot end up on a marketplace with our logo on it."

SHRED runs the project under a controlled chain of custody, with irreversible size reduction and consignment-level records — so removal from circulation is evidenced, not assumed.

Industrial site

"We've accumulated years of mixed material across the yard and no one will quote it."

SHRED assesses the site material as a defined clearance and processing project — sorting, size reduction, logistics and recovery pathways scoped and priced before work begins.

Illustrative applications. Every project is assessed individually.

Backed by Recycle Group

Anyone can buy a shredder.

What's hard is knowing where the material goes once it comes out the other side. That's where most difficult-material projects fall over.

SHRED is Recycle Group's specialist brand for customised commercial shredding and material processing. It draws on the group's shredding, granulation, crushing and size-reduction capability, and on established downstream relationships for the fractions that come out.

What that gives you

  • Method, not just machineryPreparation, processing and post-processing designed as one pathway.
  • Downstream that already existsRecovered fractions directed to established outlets rather than stockpiled.
  • Operational scaleCapacity to take on recurring contract volume, not only one-off batches.
  • A straight answerIf your material has no viable pathway, we say so at assessment stage.

You don't need a finished project brief. Tell us what the material is, roughly how much there is, where it sits and what outcome matters to you.

Photographs are the fastest place to start. A clear photo of the material and one of the storage area usually tells us more than a page of description.

We assess every submission before acceptance. If there's no technically or commercially viable pathway, we'll tell you at assessment stage — and where possible, point you at who can help.
